correctness.rationale: On the torus, differentiating (∏X_i)ΣX_i^{-1} on its zero locus gives partials proportional to X_i^{-2}; the hyperplane Jacobian condition makes them equal, so injectivity of squaring forces the all-ones point. Exactly one zero coordinate is impossible; with exactly two zero coordinates the gradient is nonzero only in the two corresponding entries, with equal nonzero value there; with at least three it vanishes. This gives the 20 distinct lines and the isolated point. Reducibility (intersection of distinct positive-degree factors) or a repeated factor would give a singular subvariety of dimension at least two in the projective hyperplane; neither occurs. The quintic hypersurface is S₂, regular in codimension one, and adjunction gives trivial dualizing sheaf. In X₅=1, the coefficient of σ_r(v) in the translation expansion of σ₅ is 6−r modulo 2; with Σv_i=0 this leaves σ₃(v)+σ₅(v). Putting v=(u₀,u₁,u₂,u₃,Σu,0) gives the two displayed homogeneous forms. The four cubic derivatives are (Σ_{j≠i}u_j)²; their common vanishing forces each u_i=Σu and hence u=0. The blowup charts have strict-transform equation Q₃(1,w)+t²Q₅(1,w)=0, smooth along the cubic; adjunction subtracts multiplicity 3 from ambient discrepancy 3. The intrinsic tangent space is Hom(ke,V/ke); e is permutation-fixed and ΣX_i³ restricts to V invariant under translation by e, so both the exceptional surface and the Segre cone base are the zero scheme of this same cubic on P(V/ke), with the same permutation action. The actual Hessian vanishes by characteristic two. The binary projective points on the quintic have weights 2, 4 and 6 (15, 15, 1), of which weights 2 and 6 are singular. Independent F₄ enumeration gives 45 cubic points (15 over F₂) and 27 lines, 15 fixed and six conjugate pairs; the classical 27-line theorem for a smooth cubic excludes further geometric lines.
residual_risks: The finite replay checks each line via five projective F₄ points, enough for vanishing of its degree-three binary restriction. It is not the geometric singular-support or smoothness proof. The singular-locus statement concerns reduced support; the resolution is only near the isolated point.

evidence: The October 26 proof explicitly identifies C by Newton as Σ_{i=0}^4 y_i³ on the slice y₅=0. In V={ΣX_i=0}, subtracting X₅e gives the unique representative with last coordinate zero in V/ke. The six-variable power sum on V is translation-invariant under ke because ΣX_i=ΣX_i²=6=0 in the relevant expansion.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Thus the descended Segre polynomial, in the same slice, is already the prior tangent equation. The tangent identification T_[e]P(V)≅Hom(ke,V/ke) with fixed generator e is canonical under permutations, so equivariance requires no new conjugacy result. Normality and adjunction follow by standard hypersurface deductions from the prior singular support. The arithmetic does not isolate a substantively new geometric claim.

originality.rationale: A distinct published catalogue record gives the same characteristic-two integral-model reduction, reduced singular support, exact local equation, smooth Clebsch exceptional cubic and crepant blowup, and further computes the local Tjurina length. The one potentially distinct comparison, the natural permutation-equivariant identification with the Segre cone base, follows directly from the prior explicit cubic on the standard tangent slice and from translation invariance of the Segre cubic on the hyperplane. The point/line counts are either acknowledged background or direct binary counts, not a surviving new structural claim. The decision is based on exact statement and equation overlap, not inaccessibility of historical literature.
residual_risks: The original 1994 Barth–Nieto article and the October 18 Resultary Segre full text were not inspected. This is not an earliest-priority determination. The broader web lookup did not complete; no negative inference is made from it.

value.rationale: Understanding the bad-reduction germ is structurally worthwhile, but the exact germ and its crepant resolution are already covered. The apparent remainder identifies two copies of the same cubic on the same tangent quotient via the coordinate slice; the checked prior equations make this a direct reformulation. The independently reproduced arithmetic consists of known cubic-surface data and a binary weight count, for which this record does not isolate a separate motivated unknown invariant.
residual_risks: This does not diminish the value of the prior geometric theorem or suggest that a genuinely new invariant of the characteristic-two quintic could not be valuable.
